aspects.says: An age in years is Period.between(birth, day).getYears(); dividing a count of days by 365 is wrong in the days before a birthday.
basis: section:Period.between Returns Fields; Count Days With ChronoUnit.DAYS.between

aspects.says: Duration.between two LocalTimes subtracts, so a span past midnight comes out negative unless a day is added.
basis: section:Duration Prints Hours, Not Days, and Its Hours and Minutes Carry the Sign

aspects.says: Duration.ofDays(1) is 24 elapsed hours while Period.ofDays(1) is the same wall-clock time on the next date, so across a DST change on a ZonedDateTime they differ by an hour.
basis: section:Duration.ofDays(1) Is 24 Hours; Period.ofDays(1) Is the Next Calendar Day

aspects.says: A Duration prints and parses ISO-8601 with hours as its largest printed field (PT48H), accepts days as 24 hours on input and refuses years, months and weeks.
basis: section:Duration Prints Hours, Not Days, and Its Hours and Minutes Carry the Sign

aspects.says: Period.between(a, b).getDays() is the days left after whole months, not the total; ChronoUnit.DAYS.between counts the total.
basis: section:Period.between Returns Fields; Count Days With ChronoUnit.DAYS.between

aspects.says: toHours() is the total hours while toHoursPart() is the hours left after whole days.
basis: section:Duration Prints Hours, Not Days, and Its Hours and Minutes Carry the Sign

aspects.says: A LocalDate has no seconds, so adding a Duration to it, or Duration.between two of them, throws UnsupportedTemporalTypeException at run time.
basis: section:Duration.ofDays(1) Is 24 Hours; Period.ofDays(1) Is the Next Calendar Day
aspects.reason: a one-line fact the page gives in its Reference; a practice would only check that the reader remembers an exception type

aspects.says: The hours, minutes and seconds parts of a negative Duration are all negative, so a label is built from the sign once and the parts of abs().
basis: section:Duration Prints Hours, Not Days, and Its Hours and Minutes Carry the Sign

aspects.says: A Period keeps the fields it was given and equals compares them, so P14M is not P1Y2M until normalized(), which folds months into years and never touches days.
basis: section:A Period Keeps the Fields It Was Given, So P14M Is Not P1Y2M

aspects.says: Schedules and calendar deadlines are Period amounts; expiries, timeouts and other elapsed time are Duration amounts.
basis: section:Duration.ofDays(1) Is 24 Hours; Period.ofDays(1) Is the Next Calendar Day
